summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic migraines, pseudotumor cerebri, hypertension, diabetes, and anxiety was admitted after a fall associated with transient loss of consciousness. She had been experiencing a persistent headache for five weeks, poorly responsive to medications including amitriptyline and opioids. Evaluation revealed no acute intracranial or cardiopulmonary pathology. CT head and MRV were unremarkable except for a chronically narrow left transverse sinus. The fall was attributed to vasovagal syncope likely triggered by pain and polypharmacy. A treatment strategy was initiated to address possible medication-overuse headache, including discontinuation of opioids and amitriptyline, and a course of high-dose steroids transitioned to oral prednisone with taper. Propranolol was reduced, and topiramate was tapered due to kidney stone risk. Her pain stabilized, and she was discharged home with follow-up planned with her headache specialist.
